description: PROBE-4 overturning check: tests whether the KL-positivity prune is airtight or only scoped to unsigned multiplicity sums. Finds the Δ_λ chirality sign = (-1)^{n(λ)} = Lusztig a-function / b-invariant parity (verified via min-maj over SYT), a cell-constant Hecke invariant that factors through the non-negative multiplicity sum — so a FORCED signed sum reproduces the mixed-sign target. Re-scopes the prune; does NOT close Δ_λ (magnitude still open).
discipline: formalize-first; no fit; exploratory probe; audit-only; does NOT wire; magnitude stays open
verdict: PROBE-4 IS SCOPED, NOT AIRTIGHT (re-scoping, no closure). The Δ_λ chirality sign sgn(w_0^{S_{λ'}}) equals (-1)^{n(λ)}, and n(λ) is the b-invariant (min major index over SYT, verified independently) = the Lusztig a-function value a_λ on the two-sided cell of V_λ (a_λ=b_λ in type A, all irreps special). Since the a-function is CONSTANT on cells, the FORCED signed multiplicity sum Σ_w (-1)^{a(w)} n^w_λ X_w = (-1)^{a_λ}·Σ_w n^w_λ X_w reproduces the exact mixed-sign target (n=3→1+/2-, n=6→6+/5-). So the prune correctly kills POSITIVE (unsigned) sums but NOT a forced a-graded signed sum: the chirality sign is the a-function/b-invariant parity, an intrinsic Hecke-cell invariant, NOT exogenous. CAVEATS (no over-claim): (a) this does NOT close Δ_λ — the MAGNITUDE Σ_w n^w_λ X_w = dim is still open; (b) (-1)^{a_λ} and sgn(w_0^{S_λ'}) are the same partition-level sign, so this RELOCATES the sign into the a-grading (writhe/framing channel), giving a derivation target rather than new content. Net: re-scope the prune from 'the sign must be exogenous' to 'the sign IS the a-function parity; the open problem is the magnitude, not the sign.'
